claims.claim: TRACE identifies candidate archaic ancestry using features of ancestral recombination graphs inferred from contemporary genomes, without requiring a sequenced archaic reference genome or an unadmixed outgroup population.
Under the authors' tested simulations and datasets, TRACE recovered known Neanderthal and Denisovan introgression signals with low reported false-discovery behavior.
The authors infer ghost archaic ancestry in both African and non-African sampled populations, consistent with gene flow before the major Out-of-Africa expansion.
The authors report approximately 0.5 to 1 percent ghost ancestry per individual in the analyzed modern-human data.
The inferred ghost source lineage diverged near the broad time depth at which the modern-human and Neanderthal-Denisovan lineages were separating, around 800,000 years ago.

The authors infer a super-archaic contribution associated with Denisovan ancestry in Oceanians, consistent with gene flow from a lineage rooted roughly 1.8 million years ago into Denisovans more than 200,000 years ago.
Scientists recovered direct DNA, fossils, or sequenced genomes from the ghost and super-archaic source populations.
The ghost ancestor was a specific named species, and the super-archaic source was definitively Homo erectus.
Every living person carries the same ghost-derived DNA segments and the same ancestry proportion.
Enrichment of inferred archaic segments near immunity and metabolic annotations proves that those segments conferred adaptive benefits.
The complete processed dataset and all intermediate ARG products required for turnkey independent reproduction are currently available from the TRACE package.

The new ghost and super-archaic source models are uniquely identified and cannot be explained by alternative demographic histories, ARG error, incomplete lineage sorting, selection, or threshold choices.

rules: Use infer, estimate, support, or detect a signal; do not use discovered fossils or sequenced the ancestor.
Do not assign a named hominin species from divergence-time overlap alone.
Do not convert population-level detection into identical ancestry for every individual.
Do not report 0.5 to 1 percent as an immutable universal value.
Do not convert genomic functional enrichment into adaptive causality.
Do not treat positive-control recovery as proof of unique identification for every latent source.
Do not declare full reproduction while processed data and exact intermediate products remain unavailable or unaudited.
